text:
Talia Benson: starting a thread for v1.1 follow-ups now that v1 is mostly stable. please dump ideas + what we’d need to validate. focus areas: refine workload buckets, add hardware variants, tighten perf thresholds.

Mateo Alvarez: +1. v1 got us to “repeatable defaults”, but the buckets are still pretty coarse. we also got burned once on mixed workload p99. let’s be more explicit.

Sofia Ivanova: biggest gap: our “mixed” bucket is basically (short prefill + long decode) only. real traffic has: long prefill bursts + short decodes, and tool/function calling patterns (lots of short turns, high churn). would like to split mixed into at least 3 buckets.

Marcus Reed: agree. right now benchmark-lab runs: short/short, short/long, long/short, long/long + one mixed. we’re missing “high concurrency chatty” (many small requests, cache hit heavy) which is where queueing policy matters.

Claire Dubois: also missing long-context edge case. we saw kernel fallback spikes on H100 when context window > ~24k w/ certain rope scaling configs (not in the matrix). even if we don’t support every combo, we should have a bucket that exercises the fallback boundary.

Hiro Tanaka: from kernel side: would like a bucket explicitly for “long prefill, low decode” since that’s where v3 attention kernel wins but also where it can blow up memory. current buckets don’t isolate it.

Omar El-Sayed: + memory. KV cache compaction thresholds behave very differently when requests are short-lived vs long-lived. fragmentation signal is way noisier in chatty patterns. we should add a “churn” bucket: many sessions start/stop.

Samir Qureshi: please yes. we tuned headroom based on steady-state-ish runs. churny alloc/free cycles are what trigger the L40S OOMs we saw in Jan. if v1.1 changes anything here we need the bucket and a guardrail threshold.

Yuki Sato: hardware variants: we should stop treating “H100” as one thing. PCIe vs SXM is showing ~5-10% throughput delta on some models, and the “best” batching default differs. also, we’ve got a small amount of H100 MIG in Dedicated (even if Hosted is no-MIG).

Neha Kapoor: infra POV: please add variants in the compatibility matrix, but keep it pragmatic. we can tag nodes with: sku=H100-SXM/H100-PCIe, mem=80g/94g (where applicable), mig=on/off, driver branch. we can’t guarantee perfect uniformity in Dedicated.

Quentin Harris: +1, but then selection rules need to acknowledge it. right now profile_id key is basically sku + cuda range + “workload bucket”. we can extend “hardware_key” to include form_factor + mig_mode.

Noah Patel: careful: exploding the profile matrix -> config drift. v1.1 proposal: add hardware variants as “constraints” and “overrides” not entirely new profiles.

Grace Kim: kernel compatibility gate already checks driver/cuda. we could add a “preferred_kernel_set” override per form factor (sxm vs pcie) without forking everything.

Allison Grant: if we add more variants, observability needs to keep cardinality under control. can we agree on 3-4 stable labels only? e.g. hw_sku, hw_form_factor, profile_id, profile_version. mig_mode maybe only emitted when not “none”.

Connor O'Brien: for release train: if v1.1 is going to tighten perf thresholds, we need to be explicit about what blocks merges vs blocks default rollout. CI gating vs rollout gates should be separate.

Sahana Iyer: +1. current perf-canary mostly warns unless delta > X%. for v1.1 we should define “hard fail” criteria for the buckets most likely to regress (mixed + churn + long-context). otherwise it’s noise.

Rina Kobayashi: benchmarking cost: adding buckets increases runtime a lot. suggestion: (1) keep full matrix nightly, (2) run a “smoke perf” subset per PR. for v1.1, choose 4 buckets for PR gating and keep the rest on nightly.

Arjun Desai: don’t forget quantization interaction: L40S runs are mostly 8-bit; H100 often FP16/BF16. buckets should annotate quant mode because cache + memory headroom differs. at least ensure each SKU gets 1 quantized bucket.

Marcus Reed: perf thresholds: right now we’re basically “no >5% p95 regression” for a couple workloads. we should tighten p99 and queueing explicitly. p99 is what triggered the incident.

Sofia Ivanova: what I’d like:
- for mixed + churn buckets: p99 latency delta threshold tighter than p95 (e.g., p99 <= +3% vs baseline)
- scheduler_queue_ms p99 absolute cap (so we catch queueing regressions even if compute is flat)
- admission control: ensure we don’t “win throughput” by letting queue grow unbounded

Omar El-Sayed: and memory thresholds:
- fragmentation_estimate should stay under X at steady state
- compaction_time_ms p95 shouldn’t spike more than Y%
- OOM rate is obviously zero in benchmarks, but we can simulate pressure by lowering headroom and ensure we degrade gracefully (admission control kicks in)

Mateo Alvarez: can we turn these into actionable items?
1) Bucket refinement proposal (owner Sofia + Marcus)
2) Hardware variants + schema tweaks (owner Quentin + Neha)
3) Threshold policy (owner Sahana + Claire + Allison)

Talia Benson: works. I’ll spin Linear issues but want rough scopes here first. also: which additional hardware variants are “must” for v1.1 vs backlog?

Neha Kapoor: must: H100-PCIe vs H100-SXM. nice-to-have: MIG on/off (but if we can just “warn + not supported” that’s acceptable for v1.1).

Hiro Tanaka: for B200: we should add at least one “B200 driver branch variance” scenario in validation. we already had mismatch issues. doesn’t need full perf gating yet, but should be in nightly.

Quentin Harris: re: B200, v1.1 could formalize “preview” profiles with explicit allowlist of driver/cuda combos. today it’s kind of hardcoded gate + docs.

Connor O'Brien: if we introduce preview profile semantics, please add clear versioning rules + changelog section (“preview: no SLA, may change defaults”). otherwise support will be confused.

Allison Grant: dashboard updates for v1.1: we should add panels for (a) bucket adoption (which buckets traffic matches), (b) scheduler_queue_ms p99 by profile_id, (c) kernel_fallback_rate by bucket + hardware_key. right now fallback is only by sku.

Grace Kim: kernel fallback rate by bucket might be super helpful. we saw fallback spikes only for long context. if we tag it, we can alert “fallback in short bucket” as a correctness smell.

Rina Kobayashi: note: to tag by bucket, benchmark runner needs to set workload_bucket label explicitly (today it’s inferred from prompt/response lengths). should be fine but needs consistency.

Sahana Iyer: tightening thresholds: can we get agreement that “p99 delta” is compared against (a) last release baseline, and (b) current default profile? we got bit when baseline was stale.

Claire Dubois: prefer baseline = “profile_version N-1 stable” for that SKU + bucket. and always log confidence intervals / rerun variance, otherwise false positives.

Marcus Reed: +1. for noisy buckets (mixed/churn) we should require 2 reruns before failing the gate.

Talia Benson: summarizing what I’m hearing:
- new/updated buckets: chatty, churn, long-context boundary, mixed split
- hardware variants: H100 form factor as must; B200 preview compatibility formalization; optional MIG handling
- thresholds: add explicit p99 + scheduler_queue_ms caps; add memory/fragmentation guardrails; separate PR smoke gating vs nightly full
I’ll draft Linear issues and link here.

Talia Benson: created:
- ENG-51xx Bucket refinement v1.1 (Sofia/MR)
- ENG-51xy Hardware variants + schema updates (Quentin/Neha)
- ENG-51xz Perf thresholds + gating policy (Sahana/Claire/Allison)
links in Linear (can’t paste from mobile rn)

Mateo Alvarez: thanks. one more ask: please include a “what could go wrong” section with each bucket change (how it might regress, what metric would catch it). we keep learning this the hard way.

Omar El-Sayed: +1, and for churn bucket specifically, define expected behavior for allocator: compaction frequency, fragmentation trend over time. otherwise people will interpret any compaction as bad.

Connor O'Brien: timeline: if we want v1.1 to land in runtime-1.23, we need bucket/spec decisions by end of next week.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, I’ll post a proposed bucket taxonomy tomorrow. will include mapping rules from live traffic -> bucket, not just benchmark definitions.

Allison Grant: please include how you want to map live traffic. we can’t rely on prompt_len/resp_len alone (tool calling is weird). maybe “turn count” or “requests per session” heuristic.

Noah Patel: (small note) anything using session heuristics needs to work in Hosted + Dedicated where session boundaries might differ. keep it optional/derived.

Talia Benson: cool. keeping thread open; drop more v1.1 ideas here as they come up.
